svg.title: Protect independent layers; restore in dependency order
svg.desc: Diagram with three parallel protection layers above four recovery stages. Protect local control-plane state using external SMB backups that survive management-cluster failure. Protect workload and application data separately; management backup does not automatically protect tenant applications. Preserve trust prerequisites, keys, certificates, configuration and approved installation media. Encryption recovery includes global Azure Key Vault access through an approved external route, not a local vault substitute. Restore prerequisites using the same root CA and externally stored decryption key. Use the documented self-service control-plane restore workflow for the same disconnected-operations version; cross-version restore is not supported. For 2609 and later, reconnect clusters present at the backup; reconnect and re-register clusters created after the backup. Verify local metadata, identity and resource bridge relationships. VM and Kubernetes workload rehydration is not automated. Recover and validate applications using their own backups.
svg.text: Protect independent layers; restore in dependency order
1-3 are parallel protection layers. 4-7 show the restore order.
Encryption recovery includes global Azure Key Vault access.
Preserve an approved external route and access outside the failed cluster.
A local vault substitute is not sufficient.
Use the same root CA and externally stored decryption key.
Confirm external SMB backup and approved global key access.
Use the documented self-service restore workflow.
Restore only to the same disconnected-operations version.
For 2609+: reconnect clusters present at the backup.
Reconnect and re-register clusters created after the backup.
Verify local metadata, identity and resource bridge relationships.
VM/Kubernetes workload rehydration is not automated.
Use workload backups; validate application data and behavior.
Test independent backup, key access and application recovery before an outage.
